pool.text: The settlement officially became a city by letters patent on July 31.
The Press was first published originally as a weekly newspaper.
New Zealand's first public railway line opened from Ferrymead to Christchurch.
Telephone service was introduced in Christchurch with New Zealand's first telephone exchange.
The city's first sewage pumping station was established in Tuam Street.
An earthquake caused the Christ Church Cathedral spire to collapse.
Cherry blossoms were planted along Harper Avenue in North Hagley Park.
A basement fire at Ballantynes department store became a major disaster.
Television broadcasts began with the launch of channel CHTV3.
Television was introduced in Christchurch with channel CHTV3.
The Lyttelton road tunnel between Lyttelton and Christchurch was opened.
Christchurch hosted the British Commonwealth Games at Queen Elizabeth II Park.
Subscriber toll dialling was introduced in Christchurch with the area code 03.
Mobile phone service was introduced to Christchurch by Telecom.
All four electricity companies entered a joint venture, named Southpower.
First Aotearoa Hip Hop Summit was held there in the city.
Pacific Underground established the Pacific Arts Festival in Christchurch.
Christchurch's Scribe released his debut album in New Zealand and received five times platinum.
The Banks Peninsula district council was amalgamated into Christchurch City.
A deadly terrorist attack targeted two mosques in the city.
